title: Draft App Documentation
text: Draft Shiny app helps users write inline reports statistical models data. displays objects user’s R environment, formats values structured lists, allows users copy setup code inline references use .qmd / .Rmd documents.

title: Draft App Documentation
text: app organized three main panels: Panel 1 (Left sidebar): Environment browser — shows registered object types scalar values Panel 2 (Centre): Object inspector — displays formatted parameters statistics inline reference paths Panel 3 (Right): Text editor + live preview — users type prose inline expressions, see live preview, copy complete .qmd chunks

title: Draft App Documentation
text: Support object class encapsulated handler registered via register_handler() R/class_*.R file. Adding new class never requires editing shared infrastructure file. handler declares: detect — whether object belongs type class_label / size_label — display strings env panel prep — converts object nested list inline use assign_result — sub-object store render_env (defaults whole result) setup_code — R code string user’s .qmd setup chunk context — Shiny input values handler needs (e.g. df mode toggle) controls — Shiny UI inspector header render — Shiny UI inspector body Registered types priority order (lower = detected first): Priority matters modelbased, performance, datawizard objects inherit data.frame; must detected dataframe handler.

title: Draft App Documentation
text: Entry point package. Captures calling environment launches Shiny app. Functions: - launch_app(env, port, launch.browser) [exported] — stores env .draft_env, registers static assets via addResourcePath(), calls shiny::runApp() - get_session_env() [exported, internal] — retrieves captured environment; used app_server access user objects

title: Draft App Documentation
text: Main server function. Manages reactive state coordinates data flow using handler registry. Type-specific logic removed — dispatch goes handlers. Key reactive state: - env_objects() — data frame user-visible objects type classifications - selected_object() — currently selected object name Panel 1 - render_env — named environment containing assigned prep lists; parent session env inline expressions can also reach raw session objects - inspector_data() — unified computed data list selected object - editor_text_d() — debounced editor text (300ms) inspector_data() unified shape (handler-based types): "scalar" "list" types (handler): simpler list type, obj, list_name. inspector_data() logic: 1. Get object env 2. classify_object(obj) → type string 3. get_handler(type) → handler 4. handler$context(input) → context list (Shiny inputs handler needs) 5. handler$prep(obj, context) → result (wrapped tryCatch) 6. Returns unified data list observeEvent(inspector_data()): - Calls handler$assign_result(result) extract sub-object store - Assigns render_env data$list_name full_chunk() reactive: - Finds registered-type objects env whose suggested list name appears editor text - Calls handler$setup_code(obj_name, list_name) referenced object - Returns complete ```{r}...``` block Helper functions: - %||% — null-coalescing operator
code: list(   type             = "parameters_model" | "effectsize" | "modelbased" | "datawizard" | "performance" | "dataframe",   result           = <output of handler$prep()>,   error_msg        = character | NULL,   list_name        = "obj_name_",   setup_code       = "obj_name_ <- draft::prep_*(obj_name)",   needs_assignment = TRUE | FALSE,   obj_class        = class(obj)[1] )

title: Draft App Documentation
text: Handles parameters_model objects — output parameters::model_parameters(). Covers frequentist Bayesian models; handles standard correlation parameter tables. Exported functions: - prep_params(params_obj) — formats parameters_model nested named list. Calls format(params_obj, zap_small=TRUE), lowercases/cleans column names, creates sanitized keys parameter column (parameter1/parameter2 correlations), calls params_df_to_list() - params_df_to_list(params) — converts formatted data frame nested list; one element per row keyed key column; skips NA / empty values Internal helpers: - is_present(x) — TRUE value non-NA non-empty string Render: - render_model_inspector(data) — reads data$result (prep output); shows one chip row per parameter; calls render_model_list_table() bottom preview Handler: priority 10, badge “P”

title: Draft App Documentation
text: Handles plain data frames tibbles. Two modes: summary (computed statistics) raw (direct $col access paths). Exported functions: - prep_data(df, cat_threshold) — summarises column; columns cat_threshold fewer unique non-missing values treated categorical (default 10) Internal helpers: - summarise_column(x, cat_threshold) — dispatches continuous categorical - is_categorical(x, cat_threshold) — classification logic - summarise_continuous(x) — returns mean, sd, median, min, max, n, n_missing - summarise_categorical(x) — returns n, n_missing, per-level n/pct sub-lists - raw_columns(df, df_name) — returns data frame column paths raw mode - column_type_label(x) — returns short type string raw mode display - render_summary_chips(summary, base) — chips single column’s summary - render_raw_columns_table(raw_df) — raw mode column list Render: - render_dataframe_inspector(data) — reads data$result$mode (“summary” “raw”); summary mode shows chip rows calls render_data_list_table() preview Handler: priority 50, badge “D”, assign_result = function(result) result$summary (summary list stored render_env, full result), context reads input$df_mode

title: Draft App Documentation
text: Handles modelbased objects: estimate_means, estimate_contrasts, estimate_slopes. Exported functions: - prep_modelbased(obj) — converts nested named list; column names never hardcoded; label columns (row identifiers) detected via attr(obj, "") character/factor columns; value columns everything numeric Internal helpers: - detect_label_cols(obj, df) — identifies identifier vs value columns - build_row_keys(df, label_cols) — builds row keys; contrasts get “Level1_vs_Level2” format; single moderator levels use level value; otherwise pastes label columns Render: - render_modelbased_inspector(data) — reads data$result; section title adapts object class (e.g. “Marginal Means”, “Contrasts”, “Marginal Effects”); calls render_modelbased_table() preview - render_modelbased_table(mb_list) — generic table; first column row key, remaining columns whatever value fields object provides Handler: priority 20, badge “MB”

title: Draft App Documentation
text: Handles effectsize package objects — object inheriting effectsize_table. Covers effectsize_difference (e.g. cohens_d, hedges_g), effectsize_anova (e.g. eta_squared, omega_squared), effectsize_table (e.g. cramers_v, phi). title: Draft App Documentation
text: Handler registry — adding new class requires R/class_*.R file; shared files need changing. aaa_ prefix aaa_handlers.R ensures sources class files package load time. Unified inspector_data() shape — handler-based types return fields (type, result, error_msg, list_name, setup_code, needs_assignment, obj_class). Handlers don’t need know . assign_result override — dataframe handler stores result$summary render_env, full result. keeps inline paths clean full result (mode, raw columns, obj reference) available rendering. Shared render helpers render_inspector_panel.R — value_chip, refer_as_bar, inspector_error, preview_table, render_model_list_*, render_data_list_* shared utilities. Class files call don’t redefine . Trailing underscore naming — suggest_list_name() returns obj_name_; underscore visually distinguishes prep list original object prose. Separation computation display — inspector_data() computes, handler$render() displays. Handlers never run prep inside render function. Priority-based detection — classify_object() walks handlers priority order subclass objects (modelbased, performance inherit data.frame) detected first.

title: Draft App Documentation
text: Test shape prep output, specific numeric values (change package versions). Check: Return type named list Length matches expected number rows/entries element named list character strings Key names follow expected pattern (e.g. _vs_ contrasts) Field name gotcha. Always discover real field names running prep function interactively writing assertions. parameters::format() returns "Coefficient" ("Estimate") lm; CI columns may "95_CI" "ci_low"/"ci_high". Use names(result$wt) inspect. Write flexible assertions fields may vary across package versions:
code: test_that("prep_mytype returns a named list", {   result <- prep_mytype(obj_a)   expect_type(result, "list")   expect_gt(length(result), 0)   expect_false(is.null(names(result))) })  test_that("each element is a named sub-list of character strings", {   result <- prep_mytype(obj_a)   for (nm in names(result)) {     expect_type(result[[nm]], "list")     for (field in names(result[[nm]])) {       expect_type(result[[nm]][[field]], "character")     }   } }) # Flexible CI check — name varies by parameters version ci_fields <- grep("ci", names(result$wt), value = TRUE) expect_gt(length(ci_fields), 0)

previous_headings: Adding Tests for a New Class
title: Draft App Documentation
text: Every class must assert prep output follows APA numeric conventions. Add block structure tests: Regex notes: - \\.[0-9]*[1-9][0-9]{2,} catches values 3+ significant decimal digits (e.g. 0.123) leading-zero values like 0.001 (1 significant decimal digit) - p-value name pattern (\\.p|^p)$ matches bare p keys unlist()-generated names like contrast_8_vs_6.p - class_parameters.R delegates parameters::format() handles conventions natively — test needs non-p check
code: # --- Formatting: decimal places --------------------------------------------  test_that("prep_mytype non-p values never exceed 2 decimal places", {   result  <- prep_mytype(obj_a)   all_vals <- unlist(result)   # Exclude p-value fields — they legitimately use 3 decimal places   p_names  <- grepl("(\\.p|^p)$", names(all_vals))   values   <- trimws(all_vals[!p_names])   values   <- values[!grepl("^[<>]", values)]   bad      <- values[grepl("\\.[0-9]*[1-9][0-9]{2,}", values)]   expect_equal(length(bad), 0L,                info = paste("Over-precise values:", paste(bad, collapse = ", "))) })  # If the class produces p-values, also assert they are APA-formatted: test_that("prep_mytype p values are APA formatted (3 dp or < .001)", {   result   <- prep_mytype(obj_a)   all_vals <- unlist(result)   p_vals   <- trimws(all_vals[grepl("(\\.p|^p)$", names(all_vals))])   # Each p-value must be a threshold string or have exactly 3 decimal places   valid <- grepl("^[<>]\\s*[0-9.]+$|\\.[0-9]{3}$", p_vals)   expect_true(all(valid),               info = paste("Badly formatted p-values:", paste(p_vals[!valid], collapse = ", "))) })

title: Draft App Documentation
text: highest-value test: exercises prep_* → assign env → render_inline() → convert_to_rmd() one chain, matching app runtime. Case preservation gotcha. summarise_categorical() uses table() preserves original case. Level "Female" produces key "Female", "female". Check actual keys names(result$col) writing string assertions.
code: test_that("value resolves in render_inline", {   result    <- prep_mytype(obj_a)   list_name <- suggest_list_name("my_obj")   first_key <- names(result)[1]    env <- new.env(parent = baseenv())   assign(list_name, result, envir = env)    first_field <- names(result[[first_key]])[1]   expected    <- result[[first_key]][[first_field]]   text <- paste0("Value: {", list_name, "$", first_key, "$", first_field, "}")    html <- as.character(render_inline(text, env, "{}"))   expect_match(html, "inline-value")   expect_match(html, htmltools::htmlEscape(expected), fixed = TRUE) })  test_that("convert_to_rmd produces correct backtick-r syntax", {   result    <- prep_mytype(obj_a)   list_name <- suggest_list_name("my_obj")   first_key <- names(result)[1]   first_fld <- names(result[[first_key]])[1]    text       <- paste0("Value: {", list_name, "$", first_key, "$", first_fld, "}.")   result_rmd <- convert_to_rmd(text, "{}")   expect_false(grepl("\\{[^`]", result_rmd))   expect_match(result_rmd, paste0("`r ", list_name, "\\$", first_key, "\\$", first_fld, "`")) })

title: Getting Started with draft
text: Writing results section means translating R objects prose, keeping prose accurate time data analysis updates, avoiding errors transcribing values data prose. draft local Shiny app makes process systematic. reads objects R environment, structures values stable named lists, gives live text editor inline references resolve type. ’re done writing, copy two things .qmd .Rmd document: small setup chunk rebuilds lists, inline references like params_m1_$wt$coefficient render correctly every time knit. draft leverages easystats suite packages (https://easystats.github.io/easystats/) systematic consistent structure, relatively dependencies, coverage many different model types analytical approaches R. draft also supports reporting bespoke dataframes create values R environment.

title: Getting Started with draft
text: draft works best alongside easystats packages. Install ones use:
code: # Install from GitHub remotes::install_github("rbcavanaugh/reproducible-reporting") install.packages(c("parameters", "effectsize", "modelbased", "performance", "correlation"))

title: Getting Started with draft
text: workflow three steps: Run analysis normally . Fit models, compute effect sizes, prepare data summaries. Open app calling draft::launch_app(). reads everything current environment. Write copy. Browse objects left panel, write prose editor, copy setup chunk inline references document. Select params_m1 environment panel. inspector shows predictor row copyable chips. Click chip copy path, paste editor, live preview renders value immediately. might write something like: Clicking Copy chunk produces setup code paste document:
code: library(draft) library(parameters)  m1        <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mtcars) params_m1 <- model_parameters(m1)  launch_app() Weight was negatively associated with fuel economy (b = {params_m1_$wt$coefficient}, 95% CI [{params_m1_$wt$ci_low}, {params_m1_$wt$ci_high}], p = {params_m1_$wt$p}). ``` r params_m1_ <- draft::prep_params(params_m1) ```

title: Getting Started with draft
text: model_parameters() main entry point regression models. works consistently across lm, glm, lmer, glmer, brms, many others — output always structure, draft handles way. inline path pattern always list_name_$term$field. Field names vary model type — frequentist models produce coefficient p; Bayesian models produce median pd. inspector always shows exact field names specific model — check rather assuming. Correlation matrices correlation package work , since correlation() returns parameters_model object: app doesn’t control statistics. Confidence levels, standardization, options stay script. use 89% CIs instead 95%: Relaunch app changing script see updated values.
code: library(parameters)  # Linear model params_lm   <- model_parameters(lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mtcars))  # Logistic regression params_glm  <- model_parameters(glm(am ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars, family = binomial))  # Mixed model library(lme4) params_lmer <- model_parameters(lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject),                                      data = sleepstudy), effects = "fixed")  # Bayesian — same workflow, different field names (median, pd instead of coefficient, p) # params_bayes <- model_parameters(brm(...)) library(correlation) corr_matrix <- correlation(mtcars[, 1:4]) # e.g. corr_matrix_$mpg_wt$r, corr_matrix_$mpg_wt$p params_lm_89  <- model_parameters(m1, ci = 0.89) params_lm_std <- model_parameters(m1, standardize = "refit")

title: Getting Started with draft
text: Effect size objects come two shapes depending function. Single-effect functions (e.g. cohens_d(), cramers_v()) return single-row result preps flat named list — path goes directly field: Multi-effect functions (e.g. eta_squared() several predictors) return one row per predictor prep nested list keyed predictor name: Conversion functions like d_to_r() return plain numeric scalars rather effectsize objects. appear environment panel scalar values (see Working scalars ).
code: library(effectsize)  es_d <- cohens_d(mpg ~ am, data = mtcars) # es_d_$cohens_d, es_d_$ci_low, es_d_$ci_high  es_v <- cramers_v(table(mtcars$cyl, mtcars$gear)) # es_v_$cramers_v_adjusted, es_v_$ci_low es_eta <- eta_squared(aov(mpg ~ cyl + gear, data = mtcars)) # es_eta_$cyl$eta2_partial, es_eta_$cyl$ci_low # es_eta_$gear$eta2_partial

title: Getting Started with draft
text: modelbased produces marginal means, contrasts, slopes — prepped named list keyed relevant level comparison. Keys come directly factor level names. Descriptive levels like "control" "treatment" produce readable paths; numeric levels like 4, 6, 8 need backtick-quoting $ paths — inspector handles automatically click chip.
code: library(modelbased)  m <- lm(mpg ~ factor(cyl) + wt, data = mtcars)  # Marginal means — one entry per level means_cyl     <- estimate_means(m, at = "cyl") # means_cyl_$`4`$mean, means_cyl_$`6`$mean  # Contrasts — keys use the _vs_ pattern contrasts_cyl <- estimate_contrasts(m, contrast = "cyl") # contrasts_cyl_$`4_vs_6`$difference, contrasts_cyl_$`4_vs_6`$ci_low  # Marginal slopes m_int      <- lm(mpg ~ wt * factor(cyl), data = mtcars) slopes_wt  <- estimate_slopes(m_int, trend = "wt", at = "cyl") # slopes_wt_$`4`$coefficient, slopes_wt_$`6`$coefficient

title: Getting Started with draft
text: model_performance() returns flat list fit indices single model. compare_performance() returns nested list keyed model name. Available indices depend model type — mixed models include ICC, logistic models include Tjur’s R². inspector shows exactly model provides.
code: library(performance)  perf_lm    <- model_performance(m1) # perf_lm_$r2, perf_lm_$aic, perf_lm_$rmse  comparison <- compare_performance(   m_null <- lm(mpg ~ 1, data = mtcars),   m_full <- lm(mpg ~ wt + cyl + am, data = mtcars) ) # comparison_$m_full$aic, comparison_$m_full$r2

title: Getting Started with draft
text: datawizard::describe_distribution() produces distribution summary table. draft supports plain (unstratified) stratified (=) forms. Unstratified — one entry per variable, flat list: Stratified — common use: one entry per group, per variable: Multiple variables supported; group keys pasted together _. Note column names dots (Sepal.Length) become compacted keys (sepallength) — check inspector exact key names.
code: library(datawizard)  dist_baseline <- describe_distribution(df[, c("age", "anxiety", "sleep")]) # dist_baseline_$age$mean, dist_baseline_$age$sd # dist_baseline_$sleep$median dist_by_condition <- describe_distribution(   df[, c("age", "sleep", "condition")],   by = "condition" ) # dist_by_condition_$control$age$mean # dist_by_condition_$treatment$sleep$sd

title: Getting Started with draft
